title: Private Deploy Telemetry & Integration Contract
author: Samira Patel
body:
Overview:

This document defines the telemetry and integration contract that Redwood Inference requires for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for customer SREs, network/security teams, and Redwood delivery engineers. The goal is to create a predictable, auditable, and minimally invasive telemetry footprint so Redwood and the customer can operate and troubleshoot the private deployment while meeting privacy and compliance constraints.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: telemetry (metrics, traces, logs), health probes, control-plane callbacks, auth for observability endpoints, retention and encryption requirements, and validation tests used during onboarding and day-2 operations.
- Audience: customer platform/SRE, customer security/compliance, Redwood deployment engineers, Redwood Support.

Design principles:
- Minimum viable telemetry: only collect what is necessary for runbookable alerts and SLA verification.
- Data minimization: avoid customer PII in telemetry; use hashed or redacted identifiers where possible.
- Configurable retention and egress: customers may opt to keep telemetry inside their VPC or allow Redwood to ingest metrics over an authenticated channel for operational support.
- Deterministic schema: metrics, span names, and log keys must follow the schemas below to allow Redwood tooling to parse and generate alerts automatically.

Prerequisites (customer responsibilities):
1) Network connectivity: (if choosing Redwood-managed observability) allow outbound TLS egress to the Redwood observability endpoint (host: obs.redwood-inference.internal OR customizable host supplied by the customer) on port 443. Alternatively, customers must provide an HTTP(S) endpoint that conforms to the schema below.
2) TLS & Auth: TLS 1.2+ enforced. Mutual TLS (mTLS) for high-sensitivity customers; otherwise Bearer token with rotating key is acceptable.
3) Time sync: NTP within ±5s across nodes.
4) Minimal system permissions: service account that can write to the provided observability endpoint and read local runtime logs.

Telemetry types and required fields:
1) Metrics (Prometheus-style time series recommended)
   - Required metric names and labels:
     - redwood.runtime.request_count{model,route,status_code} (counter)
     - redwood.runtime.request_latency_ms{model,route,p95_bucket} (histogram/summary)
     - redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio{model,route} (gauge)
     - redwood.node.cpu_utilization{node_id,zone} (gauge)
     - redwood.node.gpu_memory_used_mb{node_id,gpu_index} (gauge)
   - Labels guidance:
     - model: model identifier (e.g., gptq-13b-v1). Use the customer-visible name; avoid user IDs.
     - route: API route name (e.g., /v1/generate or /v1/chat).
     - status_code: 200, 503, 429, etc.

2) Traces (OpenTelemetry compatible)
   - Required spans and attributes:
     - Span: redwood.request (root span) with attributes: request.id, model, route, input_tokens, output_tokens, upstream_fallback (boolean), cache_hit (boolean).
     - Child spans: redwood.kv_cache.lookup, redwood.batch.serialize, redwood.kernel.exec with attributes: duration_ms, gpu_id, batch_size.
   - Sampling: default 1% sample of all requests; 100% sample of requests with status_code >= 500 and of requests explicitly flagged in the test harness. Customers may raise sampling to 10% for onboarding windows.

3) Logs
   - Structured JSON logs preferred. Log fields required for server logs:
     - timestamp (ISO8601), level (INFO/WARN/ERROR), service (e.g., runtime-agent), node_id, request_id (if request-scoped), message, error_code (if present), stack (if error).
   - Sensitive data handling: request.payload must NOT contain raw user input. If request-level context is required for debugging, the customer must supply a redacted payload or a hashed token that maps locally to the raw data under customer control.

Delivery models (customer selects one):
A) Customer-hosted observability (recommended for high compliance):
   - All telemetry is written to customer-managed endpoints inside the VPC. Redwood will provide the expected schemas and alert rules as files. Redwood support connects via ephemeral bastion and shared playbook.

B) Hybrid: Metrics & health probes are exposed to customer endpoints; Redwood ingests anonymized metrics via a secure egress channel for SLA verification. Traces and logs remain customer-hosted unless explicit permission is granted.

C) Redwood-managed ingestion: Customer allows outbound telemetry to obs.redwood-inference.internal using mTLS. This model is used for customers who want Redwood to manage alerting and incident response.

Auth and certificate management:
- mTLS: preferred for Redwood-managed ingestion. Customer provides CA or Redwood provides CSR flow and short-lived certs.
- Bearer tokens: rotate every 30 days. The token rotation endpoint is: POST /api/v1/telemetry/rotate on the customer control plane for exchange.

Schema examples:
- Metric export (Prometheus exposition format example):
  # HELP redwood_runtime_request_count Total number of requests served
  # TYPE redwood_runtime_request_count counter
  redwood_runtime_request_count{model="gptq-13b-v1",route="/v1/generate",status_code="200"} 1245

- Trace span example (OTLP JSON snippet):
  {
    "name": "redwood.request",
    "attributes": {
      "request.id": "req-2f8b",
      "model": "gptq-13b-v1",
      "route": "/v1/chat",
      "input_tokens": 32,
      "output_tokens": 128,
      "cache_hit": false
    }
  }

- Log example (single line JSON):
  {"timestamp":"2026-02-10T18:32:04Z","level":"ERROR","service":"runtime-agent","node_id":"node-17","request_id":"req-2f8b","message":"KERNEL_OOM during kernel.exec","error_code":"KERNEL_OOM"}

Operational SLOs and alerting matrix (minimum):
| Signal | SLO / Threshold | Alert | Owner |
|-------|----------------|-------|-------|
| request_success_rate (30d rolling) | >= 99.5% | page on < 99.0% | Customer SRE + Redwood on-call |
| tail_latency_p99 (in ms) | <= 2000ms for 90% of routes | alert when p99 > 4000ms for 10m | Customer SRE |
| node.cpu_utilization | <= 85% sustained | page at 95% for 5m | Customer SRE |
| kv_cache_hit_ratio | >= 70% for cacheable routes | warn below 50% for 30m | Redwood support |

Note: For customers using Redwood-managed ingestion, Redwood will create these alerts and share alert playbooks. For customer-hosted metrics, Redwood will provide the Prometheus alert rules and Grafana dashboards as IaC.

Onboarding validation checklist (run as part of deployment acceptance tests):
1) Metrics scrape: Verify Prometheus scrape of runtime endpoints returns required metrics and labels.
2) Trace sampling: Confirm traces are exported and sampled at 1% with rule exceptions.
3) Log schema: Validate structured logs against schema using the provided JSON Schema file (redwood-telemetry-log-schema-v1).
4) End-to-end test: Execute a synthetic request that triggers kernel.exec and verify corresponding metric increment, trace span, and log entry appear within 60s.
5) Auth & certs: Rotate telemetry token and verify 401 -> 200 transition on key update.

Upgrade and rollback considerations for telemetry:
- During upgrades, retain dual-schema compatibility for 2 minor releases. All new metric names must be introduced alongside the old names for 30 days with telemetry tags indicating version.
- Rollback steps must include backfilling any missing metric where a rename occurred: a shim exporter can write the legacy metric name for 48 hours after rollback.

Day-2 operational playbook excerpt (high level):
1) Incident triage:
   - Step 1: Confirm alerts (metrics/trace/log).
   - Step 2: Identify node and request_ids via traces or logs.
   - Step 3: If kernel OOM or node-level resource saturation, scale GPU pool or trigger failover policy (see customer-specific HA doc).
   - Step 4: If unavailable, engage the Redwood on-call via the secure channel and provide sanitized request_ids and time windows.

2) Routine maintenance:
   - Rotate telemetry tokens on a 30-day cadence.
   - Verify scraping and ingestion post-maintenance within 15 minutes.
   - Run the synthetic end-to-end test after each major package upgrade.

Data retention and compliance options:
- Default retention: metrics 90 days (aggregated to 1d after 30 days), traces 30 days (sampled), logs 30 days.
- Customer can request retention changes; any retention >365 days requires a compliance exception and approval from legal/security.

Escalation and ownership:
- First responder: Customer SRE (documented in the customer runbook supplied at handoff).
- Second line: Redwood deployment engineer (on-call) with access to anonymized telemetry and runbook.
- Third line: Redwood runtime engineering for kernel-level faults.

Deliverables from Redwood to customer:
- Prometheus scrape configuration (YAML) and alert rule set.
- Grafana dashboards (JSON) for runtime, nodes, and caches.
- Trace sampling and span processor config (OTLP/collector config).
- Telemetry validation harness (Python script) used during onboarding.

Appendix A — Example Prometheus job snippet:
  scrape_configs:
    - job_name: "redwood-runtime"
      static_configs:
        - targets: ["10.0.2.15:9100"]
      metrics_path: /metrics
      scheme: https
      bearer_token_file: /etc/redwood/telemetry-token

Appendix B — Minimum dashboard panels to include:
- Requests per second (per model)
- P95/P99 latency (per route)
- KV cache hit ratio over time
- GPU memory used and utilization per node
- Trace-error waterfall for failed requests
